cls: Antineoplastic - HER2/neu receptor antagonist (anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody)
pharm: Recombinant humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular dimerization domain (subdomain II) of HER2, blocking ligand-dependent HER2 heterodimerization (especially with HER3) and inhibiting downstream signaling; complements trastuzumab in HER2-positive breast cancer.
quick: Loading 840 mg IV, then 420 mg IV every 3 weeks (with trastuzumab and chemotherapy)
Intravenous infusion; not related to meals

Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose
No adjustment for mild to moderate impairment; not studied in severe
Not formally studied; no specific dose adjustment provided

summary: Pertuzumab is a recombinant humanized IgG1 anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody used in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy for HER2-positive breast cancer - in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings for early-stage disease and as first-line treatment of metastatic disease. The recommended dose is an initial loading dose of 840 mg IV followed by 420 mg IV every 3 weeks, given with trastuzumab and chemotherapy. It carries a BOXED WARNING for left ventricular dysfunction/cardiomyopathy (decreases in left ventricular ejection fraction) - assess LVEF at baseline and every 3 months during treatment and withhold for significant declines - and for EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY, which can cause fetal harm including oligohydramnios, oligohydramnios sequence, and death; effective contraception is required. Pertuzumab blocks HER2 dimerization and complements trastuzumab's distinct mechanism.
indications: Neoadjuvant treatment of HER2-positive, locally advanced, inflammatory, or early-stage breast cancer (tumors >2 cm or node-positive) as part of a complete regimen for early breast cancer, in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy
Adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy

First-line treatment of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel, in patients who have not received prior anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease

dosage.d: Initial loading dose 840 mg, then 420 mg every 3 weeks
dosage.n: Always given with trastuzumab and chemotherapy

dosage.d: 420 mg infused over 30 to 60 minutes every 3 weeks
If <6 weeks since last dose, give 420 mg as soon as possible; if >=6 weeks, re-administer the 840 mg loading dose, then resume 420 mg every 3 weeks

admin: Administer as an intravenous infusion only; do not give as an IV push or bolus
Give the 840 mg loading dose over 60 minutes; give the 420 mg maintenance dose over 30 to 60 minutes
Dilute in 250 mL of 0.9% Sodium Chloride; do not use dextrose solutions; do not shake; do not mix with other drugs
Administer with trastuzumab and chemotherapy; pertuzumab and trastuzumab may be given in any order, but chemotherapy (e.g., docetaxel) should generally be given after the antibodies
Observe the patient for 30 to 60 minutes after the first infusion and 30 minutes after subsequent infusions for infusion-associated and hypersensitivity reactions
Withhold or discontinue for significant LVEF decline; manage infusion/hypersensitivity reactions by slowing or stopping the infusion
moa: Pertuzumab is a recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody (IgG1) that targets the extracellular dimerization domain (subdomain II) of the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). By binding this region, it blocks ligand-dependent heterodimerization of HER2 with other HER family members, particularly HER3. This inhibits the downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways, leading to cell growth arrest and apoptosis. Pertuzumab also mediates antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Because it targets a HER2 epitope distinct from that bound by trastuzumab, the two antibodies provide complementary, more comprehensive HER2 signaling blockade when used together.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to pertuzumab or any of its excipients
relative: Pre-existing left ventricular dysfunction or significant decline in LVEF (cardiomyopathy risk)
Prior cardiotoxic therapy (e.g., anthracyclines) or chest radiation
History of significant infusion or hypersensitivity reactions to HER2-directed antibodies
monitor: Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and every 3 months during treatment (boxed warning)
Signs and symptoms of heart failure
Pregnancy status before initiating in females of reproductive potential

preg: BOXED WARNING: Exposure to pertuzumab during pregnancy can result in embryo-fetal harm, including oligohydramnios and oligohydramnios sequence manifesting as pulmonary hypoplasia, skeletal abnormalities, and neonatal death. Verify pregnancy status before initiating in females of reproductive potential and advise patients of the risk to the fetus. Use effective contraception during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of pertuzumab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Human IgG is excreted in milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child, advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. Pertuzumab has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment; no dosing recommendation can be made.
hepatic: The pharmacokinetics of pertuzumab in patients with hepatic impairment have not been studied, and no specific dosage adjustment is provided in the labeling.

major: Anthracyclines and other cardiotoxic agents - additive risk of left ventricular dysfunction; sequence and monitor LVEF carefully
moderate: Trastuzumab (used concurrently by design) - shared cardiotoxicity; monitor cardiac function
Concomitant chemotherapy (e.g., docetaxel) - overlapping myelosuppression and toxicity
minor: No clinically significant cytochrome P450-mediated small-molecule interactions established (monoclonal antibody); no PK interaction observed between pertuzumab and trastuzumab or docetaxel
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction with alcohol established.
interactions.diagnostics: Confirm HER2 overexpression with an FDA-approved test before use; assess LVEF (echocardiogram or MUGA) at baseline and every 3 months; verify pregnancy status before initiation.

common: Peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia (in combination with chemotherapy)
serious: Left ventricular dysfunction / cardiomyopathy (decreased LVEF, congestive heart failure)
Embryo-fetal toxicity (oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, skeletal abnormalities, neonatal death)
Severe febrile neutropenia and neutropenic infection (with chemotherapy)
rare: Severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte disturbance
emergency: Symptomatic heart failure / significant LVEF decline

monitoring: Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and every 3 months during treatment; withhold for clinically significant decreases (boxed warning)
Signs and symptoms of congestive heart failure
Infusion-associated and hypersensitivity reactions during and after each infusion
Complete blood count for neutropenia when given with chemotherapy
Pregnancy status before initiation in females of reproductive potential
counsel: This medicine can weaken the heart - tell your doctor right away about shortness of breath, swelling of the ankles/legs, cough, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or unusual tiredness; you will have regular heart scans
It can seriously harm an unborn baby - use effective birth control during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose, and tell your doctor immediately if you become or may be pregnant
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose
Report reactions during the infusion such as fever, chills, flushing, rash, trouble breathing, or low blood pressure
Diarrhea is common - stay hydrated and contact your care team if it is severe or persistent
pk: Steady-state concentrations reached by the third dose with the loading/maintenance schedule
Intravenous administration achieves peak serum concentration at end of the infusion
Every-3-week dosing maintains therapeutic exposure; re-load if interval exceeds 6 weeks
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C (36-46 F) in original carton to protect from light; do not freeze or shake; use diluted solution per labeling
pearls: BOXED WARNING: cardiomyopathy / left ventricular dysfunction - assess LVEF at baseline and every 3 months, withhold for significant decline, and discontinue if LVEF does not recover

BOXED WARNING: embryo-fetal toxicity (oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, neonatal death) - verify pregnancy status and ensure effective contraception during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose
Always given as part of a regimen with trastuzumab and chemotherapy; never as monotherapy for breast cancer
Dosing: 840 mg loading then 420 mg every 3 weeks - re-administer the 840 mg loading dose if the interval since the last dose is 6 weeks or more
Targets a different HER2 epitope (dimerization domain) than trastuzumab, providing complementary HER2 blockade
missed: There is no patient self-administered dose. If a planned infusion is missed: when less than 6 weeks have elapsed since the previous dose, give the 420 mg maintenance dose as soon as possible; if 6 weeks or more have elapsed, re-administer the 840 mg loading dose over 60 minutes and then resume 420 mg every 3 weeks. The oncology team manages rescheduling.
overdose: No maximum tolerated dose of pertuzumab has been determined, and single doses higher than 25 mg/kg have not been tested. In case of overdose, monitor the patient closely for signs or symptoms of adverse reactions, particularly cardiac dysfunction, and institute appropriate symptomatic treatment.
